name: Virgin Prunes
label: Rough Trade
lede: Lypton Village in north Dublin produced two bands. One became U2; the other wore dresses and plastic suits, got pulled off a Clash support slot and talked Rough Trade into a record that came as a 7-inch, a 10-inch, a 12-inch, a cassette, a book and a film.

eras.title: The other Lypton Village band
eras.text: Lypton Village was a gang of north Dublin teenagers who gave each other new names and lived by their own rule: art, music and weirdness good, everything else bad. Fionan Hanvey became Gavin Friday, Derek Rowen became Guggi, Paul Hewson became Bono. The Village had two house bands, and the Virgin Prunes took the avant-garde half. Their stage shows got them banned from venues and, after a Late Late Show appearance, from RTÉ.

years.src: Irish Times: Gavin Friday · Mute: Virgin Prunes · gavinfriday.com: Prune power
years.h: Friday, Guggi and Dave-iD front a band with three singers
years.p: Behind them: Dik Evans, brother of the Edge, on guitar; Guggi's brother Trevor, now Strongman, on bass; Pod on drums. Evans had played in the early U2.
years.xp: Friday, Guggi and Bono called themselves "the three mouths." Friday told the Irish Times all three had difficult relationships with their fathers, "who by sheer coincidence were all called Robert." Later the two bands shared bills at the Dandelion Market under the banner "U2 Can Be A Virgin Prune."

years.src: gavinfriday.com: When art and anarchy collide
years.h: For gig number two, U2 are the backing band
years.p: Friday wears a suit made out of plastic raincoats and Guggi a tiny skirt, with the band then called the Hype behind them.

years.cap: The Virgin Prunes in Hot Press, A Sense of Ireland, London
years.src: gavinfriday.com: When art and anarchy collide
years.h: The Clash's tour manager drags them off the Top Hat stage
years.p: Opening for [[The Clash|8f92558c-2baa-4758-8c38-615519e9deda]] in Dún Laoghaire, Friday's plastic suit splits and Guggi's skirt comes off. Bottles fly and a curtain catches fire.
years.xp:
Friday's summary: "all hell broke loose." Later, he said, the front rows filled up with Gavin and Guggi clones.

Steve Averill of the Radiators From Space played synthesizer with them in those early days.

eras.title: A new form of beauty, £6,000 of photos
eras.text: With Pod gone and Haa-Lacka Binttii on drums and tape loops, the Prunes signed to Rough Trade and started their own Baby label. For about two years they were as productive as they were difficult: a multi-format art project, a French box set made in three sleepless days, and a debut produced by Wire's Colin Newman.

years.p: The first single comes out on the band's own Baby Records, distributed by Rough Trade, and reaches No. 25 on the UK indie chart. Moments and Mine follows in June.

years.h: Binttii is pushed out and his name comes off the credits
years.p: After fights with the others, Binttii leaves; Mary D'Nellon takes the drums and some of Binttii's parts are re-recorded. Binttii goes on to Princess Tinymeat.

years.src: gavinfriday.com: When art and anarchy collide · Wikipedia: Virgin Prunes · Mute: Virgin Prunes
yt: The band on A New Form of Beauty
years.h: Rough Trade asks for an album and gets A New Form of Beauty
years.p: Geoff Travis wanted an album with a producer. The Prunes offered a 7-inch, 10-inch, 12-inch and cassette, plus a gig, a film and a book, and the label got angry about the photo bill.
years.xp:
The four parts came out from October 1981 to February 1982; parts 1 and 2 made the indie chart at Nos. 44 and 47. The book, A New Form of Beauty 6, was never published and the film, part 7, was never released.

Mute later described the idea as the beauty of being different, physically and musically, the same idea Lypton Village was built on.

years.src: Mute: Virgin Prunes · Wikipedia: Virgin Prunes
years.p: It reaches No. 13 on the UK indie chart, the Prunes' best showing for a single.

years.src: Wikipedia: ...If I Die, I Die · virginprunes.com: Brief history
years.h: Colin Newman of Wire produces the debut at Windmill Lane
years.p: Recorded in Dublin in July and August, ...If I Die, I Die comes out on Rough Trade and reaches No. 8 on the indie chart. Baby Turns Blue goes ahead of it in October.
years.xp: The line-up: Friday and Dave-iD on vocals with Guggi, Dik Evans on guitar, Strongman on bass, D'Nellon on drums. Claude Bessy called the Prunes' sound a roller coaster through [[Throbbing Gristle|e135d690-9c53-4333-8f11-98aec8c9f434]] with Stooges-style string-bending.

years.src: Mute: Virgin Prunes · Wikipedia: Virgin Prunes
years.h: A Paris label pays for a box set about insanity
years.p: Yann Farcy of L'Invitation au Suicide commissioned Hérésie after seeing the band at the Rex Club. They wrote by day and recorded by night, three days without sleep.

eras.title: Touring it to death
eras.text: Germany and Scandinavia took to them early, and from 1982 to 1985 the band toured Europe and the US East Coast. Friday says the road wore everyone out. Guggi and Dik Evans left, an album was abandoned, and the one that finally came out sounded like nobody's idea of goth.

years.src: Mute: Virgin Prunes · gavinfriday.com: Prune power
years.h: On the road, and keeping clear of goth
years.p: The Prunes built one of the first overseas followings for an Irish punk-era band. Mute's history says they pushed back on goth because it was about image, not individuality.

years.src: Irish Times: Gavin Friday · gavinfriday.com: When art and anarchy collide · Wikipedia: Virgin Prunes
years.h: Guggi leaves to paint and Dik Evans follows
years.p: D'Nellon moves to guitar and Pod comes back on drums. The album they start, Sons Find Devils, is abandoned.
years.xp: Friday said the rhythm section wanted to be in a straight rock 'n' roll band; he was drifting toward Brecht and Weill and Jacques Brel. Guggi became a painter.

years.src: Mute: Virgin Prunes · Wikipedia: Virgin Prunes
years.h: Over the Rainbow clears out the vaults
years.p: Baby's compilation of rarities from before 1983 reaches No. 22 on the indie chart and shows how far the band had ranged: industrial, krautrock, glam.

years.src: Mute: Virgin Prunes · Wikipedia: Virgin Prunes
years.h: Dave Ball of Soft Cell produces a record of ballads
years.p: Recorded in 1984 and out two years later as a four-piece, The Moon Looked Down and Laughed leans on European chanson. It reaches No. 5 on the indie chart; Touch and Go puts it out in the US.
play: The Moon Looked Down and Laughed

years.big: "It always had to be a short lived thing."
q: One of the purest bands ever to come out of this country.
years.src: gavinfriday.com: When art and anarchy collide · Irish Times: Gavin Friday · virginprunes.com: Brief history
years.h: Gavin Friday leaves, and the Virgin Prunes are over
years.p: Friday, looking back in 2009. A short note on the sleeve of the 1987 live album The Hidden Lie, recorded in Paris on June 6, 1986, makes the end official.
years.xp:
Friday blamed the constant touring, which he said "basically killed the band," and the gap left by the founders: "Sorry as I was to leave, I just couldn't go on without Dik and Guggi."

He still calls them one of the purest bands ever to come out of Ireland.

eras.title: Prunes, scores and Carnegie Hall
eras.text: The rhythm section kept a shortened name going for three albums. Friday went solo and into film scores, often with Bono, and the old band came back in pieces: on Mute reissues and, for two songs, at Carnegie Hall.

years.h: D'Nellon, Strongman and Dave-iD carry on as the Prunes
years.p: Lite Fantastik (1988, with Dik Evans playing), Nada (1989) and Blossoms & Blood (1991), the last with 17-year-old Justin Kavanagh of Dublin hardcore band Mutant Asylum on guitar.

years.h: Friday's first solo album, then film scores with Bono
years.p: Each Man Kills the Thing He Loves comes first. With Maurice Seezer and Bono he scores In the Name of the Father (1993), The Boxer and In America, which earned a Golden Globe nomination.

years.cap: Gavin Friday at the Clarence Hotel, Dublin
years.src: Mute: Virgin Prunes · Wikipedia: Virgin Prunes
years.h: Mute reissues the catalogue, remastered under Friday's eye
years.p: Five CD packages, with previously unheard mixes. Over the Rainbow returns as a double CD of rarities from 1980–84.

years.cap: Friday with Courtney Love at Carnegie Hall, New York, 4 October 2009
years.src: Wikipedia: Virgin Prunes · gavinfriday.com: Prune power
years.h: Friday, Guggi and Evans play two Prunes songs at Carnegie Hall
years.p: At Friday's 50th birthday concert they play Sweethome Under White Clouds and Caucasian Walk, with J.G. Thirlwell singing backup. All four members of [[U2|a3cb23fc-acd3-4ce0-8f36-1e5aa6a18432]] perform that night too.

q: I think me and Guggi are bolder boys.
years.h: "Bolder boys" than Bono and the Edge
years.p: Friday tells the Irish Times he and Guggi are bolder than their famous friends, down to temperament rather than strategy. He calls the Prunes' music "risqué, avant-garde."
